brief: The Market Ear compiles eight unconnected charts the note frames as 'extremes,' with no single argument tying them together. Ericsson now trades at a 50% valuation premium to Nvidia, which the note frames as ironic given Ericsson's dot-com-era peak. Hedge fund positioning in AI stocks has fallen back to summer-2023 levels, when Anthropic was valued near $5 billion. AI capex is expected to reach $1.3 trillion in 2027 even as free cash flow among the spenders runs -$283 billion. Semiconductor earnings-revisions breadth is rolling over, presented sarcastically to undercut the idea that chip earnings are no longer cyclical. The S&P 500's 493 non-Mag7 members are outgrowing the Mag7 in EPS for the first time since Q4 2022, a trend analysts expect to continue in Q4 (30.8% versus 24.1%). The note also cites a decade of S&P 500 forward P/E contractions, Morgan Stanley's Global Risk Demand Index sitting in 'clear fear territory,' and investment-grade yields now exceeding the S&P 500's earnings yield by the widest margin since the early 2000s, with less volatility.
